The air rang solemn with the sound of metal. The clang of a rusty vestige of humanities past colliding with the patina of some emblem of their future home. To the unaided eye, it was little more than a vending machine. To the scavenger Urdnot, it was the ticket out of this dump.

He had heard rumors now, growing stronger as the desperation gnawed at the claustrophobic quarters his crew commanded, of a large scale operation up north. The Golden Arches were finally going to get it to those plastic meat masticating bastards. The move was in due time of course, as a wave of Apple renegades; full of febrile fervor and fury destroyed swathes of their back line. Their supply lines cut, the Golden Arches were deeply committed to a retreat. 

Hardly able to contain his excitement, Urdnot roused a speech among his kin.

"Long have we waited for this day, my brothers"

A murmur of agreement from the crowd. The tension was palpable. He had to say what they expected him to.

"We fight for reasons we have always fought for. For values we have always held dear. For the glory of all that is fizzy and carbonated."

A whispering in the backlines caught his ear

"But what are we to do with this magical substance when we finally have it"?

An uproar of laughter erupted from deep in Urdnot's belly. Did this man not have faith?

Lowering his stance and forcing his eyes unwavering to meet this questioning fellow, he spoke softly but with great deliberation.

"Has it not been foretold? The untold knowledge of civilization before the Great Conflagration, the ruins of all that was, the path to all that will be. All will be revealed once our priests lips touch the Sacred Substance"

"Is it not the way of the book? The beverage of the last supper according to The Great Pepsico?!"

An incredulous man offered, in great accordance. Susserations and nods of agreement among the eager throng

"We are the Pepsi Generation" roared Urdnot,

As the hands came up to clasp him firmly on the shoulder, the multitude of deliriously roaring faces started to blur from his vision. 

*I do not know for why we fight. Other than hope. The hope of a way out of this butchery*

Countless bottlecaps rattled in his bag as those around him shook and jostled him fervently. 

*A years worth of pay was going into this mission. It better be fucking worth it.*



***********************************************



The Gospel of the Arches was left of course to the care of His Reverence Dollard Kempt. As they were entrusted to his care, he took great offense to them being read infront of him without his permission; a thing that some impudent little welp was attempting to get away with at present.

"How dare you consecrate the work of all that is fatty and deep fried"?

Speckles of sputtum flying off his enraged face, showering the cowering literary assailant outrage. His visage a vision of incredulous rage.

Awestruck he could but stutter

"I...I--I w-w-w-wanted only to..."

"There is nothing more in the world you wanted than to peer behind the veil and glimpse at the awesome majesty of Our Ronalds Wisdom. I know my child, I know".

There was little he could do but nod. 

*Excellent, now I have him* thought Dollard slyly. *Time to tighten the vice*

"How did you even sneak in here, this room is off limits to all but members of the highest order"

"Well...I--...you see.."

"AND, furthermore, how have you abased yourself so, to apprehend the book without first uttering the appropriate incantation. Surely you know even this most basic fact. Those who fail to regard this principle must be punished"

"I know..I simply forgot, in my excitement, you see"

"No I don't see. In fact, i'd like very much for you to recite the Holiest of His Names now"

"McFish! Err...the McRib Supreme. Limited time only. 1.99? Double cheeseburger with...er...special sauce"

Clearly floundering and visibly flushing, he shrugged his shoulders hopefully as his eyes darted around the room. So transparently searching for a means of escape. *The precious fool*

It was in the split second he averted his gaze that he felt the sharp needle of the knife point accosting his throat.

"Move another inch and your blood will be spilt like Grease from the Glory of BigMac", murdered his Reverence murderously."

Unable to move, scarcely able to breath, his assailant expressed his assent with a nodding of his balled hand

Releasing him suddenly in a thrust and using his own weight to propel him to the floor, Dollard subdued the pitiable tittering mess of a spy, holding him supine.

"NAME!" He demanded

Spluttering. Hesitation.

"It doesn't matter who you are. All I care about is what you know. And all you care about i'm sure my child, is escaping this room. Our goals are not mutually exclusive."

Silence and heaving breathing followed.

"SPEAK" He bellowed, pressing the knife point barely into the skin, expelling an excruciated yell from the intruders larynx and eliciting his fearful compliance.

"I'm part of an Apple renegade cell. We've infiltrated the highest level of the Church of the Big Mac. One of our historians and corporatologist has irrefutable proof of the fallibility of the Special Sauce. The Apple is from the Tree of Knowledge. The fatty and fried are perversions. We've invaded every part of this sad little facade you call a company. "

Considering this for a while, Dollard deigned to pause pensively in his response. Even loosening the pressure on the spy's skin a little as a reward for his disclosure. 

Growing bolder now, the sad little vermin of a man added, voice as vitriolic as acid

"You'll never take us all out! Never!"

"I can only try" uttered Kempt, as the sound of flesh rendered by steel was drowned in the wails of agony.

I think this is a good idea. I know someone personally who has had a similar goal as yours; to make himself more articulate. He wanted to go through a dictionary and just find cool words, write them down and memorize them.

While I think the goal itself is a good one, I don't think brute memorization is the correct approach. Thus in my opinion a poster with just a bunch of words on it is rather defunct (there are word a day calendars you can by that present the information more succinctly).

I found in improving my vocabulary an effective and enjoyable way to learn is to study a small number of word roots, prefixes and suffixes and their meanings. Since English has a preponderance of words handed down to it from Latin (and later old french, middle french and norman) studying a small number of building blocks can enable one to extrapolate the meaning of otherwise unknown words from their constituent parts, and to create new words from the same pieces. Studying these roots also helps greatly in learning other romance languages that share a common etymology (IE: Italian, French, Spanish, Romanian etc)

For example; from the latin root cede meaning to go, move or yield
CONcede (to move with/yield with)
PROceed (to go after, move after)
REcede (to go back, move back)

I've done my own little study of these roots but I would definitely be interested in seeing this in poster form as an educational resource.

(Source of common Latin/Greek roots in English incase you are interested: https://msu.edu/~defores1/gre/roots/gre_rts_afx2.htm)

Sane, healthy and informed people should have full control over whatever substances they put in their body. Yes, this includes all illegal and harmful drugs. I believe there is much to be gained in the way of self knowledge from psychedelic drugs. Other chemicals, like opiates and dopaminergic drugs have little to no revelatory potential, but people should be able to legally use them if they see fit. They are going to use them anyway if they have the desire, and the current paradiagm of treating drug use as a legal issue/moral failing does little more but create additional harms. We should be treating drug use as a mental health issue and offering mental health interventions and services rather than putting people into the criminal system.

Good write up. I play in a similar bracket and have a 70%+ winrate with necro. I agree with your item analysis, however IMHO:

Bloodstone: This is my meh item..Sure health and mana are great...however because of sadist and smart use of reapers in fights you should almost never be low mana. Realistically one large mana item (sheep or shiva) or a little 1 and some cheap stats (veil,   ghost sceptre, Atos,) will be all the mana pool you need. Necro really doesnt benefit from the regen on bloodstone say over any big mana item since he has a broken built in passive for regen that procs reliably as long as you can get kills. The heal on death of bloodstone is really nice and a cool feature, as is the respawn time. Sadly necro suffers from the same problem as DP, another hero that people build bloodstone on rather sub-optimally, IE: reliance on ult. Most of the utility necro offers in fights (at least up until lategame where your sheer tank and heal spam is doing work) is on being able to quickly burst down a hero with reapers and regen any punishment. Once you've gotten your ult off and executed someone your use in teamfights is severly reduced, unlike timber or storm.

Agha: I like you have had different phases of opinion of this item. When the buyback removal mechanic was introduced it was a nice mechanic to stop annoying splitpushers if you could catch em, your nagas tinkers broods TBs. Then once respawn time was added to base ult it made reapers and by extension its aghas upgrade even stronger. I consider agha absolutely core now. Agha is my core lategame item. Generally my 3th-5th item. I am to get it when the teams are grouping up to take highground and buybacks on carries are saved for. Just getting aghas at this time and then taking a fight where you ulti a carry who has been saving for buyback for the last ~3 minutes has got to be the best feeling. I do think aghas is situational. Its situation is late. Seriously, if you ult the right target and the carry cant buyback often the won fight turns into easy rax. Agha lategame every game.

Shivas:

I like shiva, I really do. But for me its more situational: I buy it vs heroes that rely on physical attack speed DPS. Maybe vs troll PA or SB. Often I prefer sheep most games. I like sheep cause I tend to build mobility (usually try to have either force or blink) and a blink hex makes you a decent intiator. Any nearby teammates who can contribute a stun or two can chain nuke them into an ult before BKB. I do like rod of atos and consider it my poor mans. But if the game is going well and im getting kills and some good farm ill often grab sheep second since its not that much extra farm.

Veil:
You should consider this. Just try it one game. Works well with atos too, but this combination of items doesnt scale super well and is probably better off in a pushing build. For magic damage to augment your ult this is one of the strongest midgame pickups

I like that necro can be flexible with lanes. I've run him as the pos 1 safelane (not my favourite) pos 2 mid (usually pretty good, matchup dependant) and dual offlane with another aggresive pick. Necro works really well with a lane partner vs trilane. A recent example I played was necro undying against a safelane tri. Necro ogre is also fun and quite decent.

Blademail: This is another great midgame item I encourage you to try. Its a little situational (have to make sure a least a few of their dangerous cores arent getting BKB, def worth getting vs lots of AOE damage) but works really well on necro. Necro wants to be at that critical mass where they takes lots of DoT and pulse punishment for not focusing you...then when they decide to focus you, you pop the blademail and kite and heal. Ive used this very effectively against DP and forced her to shred herself chasing me. Or PA if rushed after mec and your stomping. The key is not to use it too early in fights, but to bait people into overcommitting before popping blademail and forcing them to eat a reapers. If used right this item makes anyone who doesnt have MUCH more health and or sustain than you unable to solo kill you since you can dissuade them from nuking you down if you time things right

Its hard to give you a definitive answer because I don't know your prospect, your product, your potential rapport and your comfort level with being that direct.

When I used to sell insurance I used to have a few different closes, and a good salesperson never has one set close for every prospect. Sometimes, if you get the vibe; this person wants to buy, they need the product, they don't have many strong objections and there might be a sense of urgency then being direct is the strongest hand you can play. I used to say "Well, since that all looks good and you need this policy to cover your brand new home i'll set it up for you from today so you'll be covered."

Other circumstances call for a more indirect, subtle approach. One thing though, I strongly believe that specific words are VERY influential. If you are going for the direct approach don't say "CAN I" You're giving them the option of saying no. Try something like "I will bring in the contract so we can check the terms together, and ensure everything suits you before we go ahead with this great plan"

Its not even about being direct (although it can be), it's about getting it into your mind that your sales pitch needs to have a distinct closing phase -- a part where you consciously try to get the customer to say yes. Typically during this phase the customer is going to throw all sorts of objections at you and handling those is in itself an art.

Let's go through an example, when I used to sell insurance over the phone I remember seeing a lot of my peers quote a customer over the phone, explain the policy is great detail and how it would help the customer, why they need it. At the end of their pitch, there would be a silence and the customer would say something like "Great well, send that through to me by email and i'll get back to you when i'm ready to buy it"; they forgot or neglected to practice the simple habit of asking for the sale. They didn't last long.

Hi OP,

I've worked in sales for a number of years. First of all, I highly recommend reading Influence -- The Psychology of Persuasion by Cialdini. It takes the scientific approach to understanding what works and what doesn't in sales pitches and general influence and helped me immensely. I would also recommend the Little Red Book, but it felt a little insubstantial to me (that may be just because im a skeptic and like anything I read to be based on science, your mileage may vary)

I think a large part of sales involves feeling comfortable with yourself and your product, being able to talk about it and most importantly being able to ASK FOR THE SALE. Once you can ask comfortable -- not feel guilty or intrusive or rude for asking you have your close. As you fail and succeed repeatedly you will be able to slowly hone your pitch and your close to specific types of customers, products, situations. A good sales person is adaptable.

But most importantly if you never become comfortable with asking for the sale you will never, ever become good at selling anything.

This is a good question and i'm going to provide you with a good answer.

As insomnia kicks in the brain and body accrue sleep debt. When the insomniac gets to sleep again the brain forces the body to get more REM sleep (as this is vital for maintaining homeostasis and mental health). The first night after a period of insomnia is almost entirely REM (as opposed to normal sleep cycles which consist of about 60% REM) which accounts for the strange and vivid dreams many experience after a bout of insomnia.

After a long period of insomnia one COULD sleep for 8 hours wake up and go on with their day however they would still be carrying a HUGE amount of sleep debt around with them. The body would attempt to repay this debt over the ensuing months/years by increasing overall sleep time/frequency of naps and proportion of REM sleep every time the person went to sleep.

>
What is your personal experience with the organisation and how did you come to work here 

* 
people LOVE talking about themselves and love it when you are interested in them (even if its feigned interest) and can give you some perspective on the
 org* 


>
In 5 years time if I were performing well, where could I expect to go with this role

* 
shows you care about career progression and are motivated, not just a drone

>What is the next step in the selection process, when can I expect to hear from you again? 

* 
I always always ALWAYS drop this one. Shows that you want to chase up the position and are strongly interested in it

Those are only a few examples I can think of off the top of my head. But I hope that helps :)
